messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on continuous-batching and the tiny-request regressions we've seen. I want to capture options and get consensus on the admission API boundary.
aj: Thanks. What's the simplest thing that fixes the tail without huge runtime surgery?
maria: Short term: add a tiny-size hint to the admission call so the scheduler can route without guessing. Long term: either virtual-batching in scheduler or kernel-level aggregation.
sam: The problem right now is adapters lost the cohorting hints after the adapter split. Lots of 1-2 token requests end up in the default lane and cause early coalesce drains.
chris: If we expose a hint, we must keep it intentionally small. Too many fields -> SDK churn and coupling. Maybe a single enum + optional deadline.
nina: We should also consider a no-API-change path: adapters set request metadata in tracing/context and admission reads it. Cleaner rollout but it's leaky across layers.
maria: Tradeoffs: explicit hint = clear contracts, easier tests; context metadata = fast but brittle and harder to audit. Prefer explicit minimal change.
elje: elaine: Another axis is enforcement: even with a hint, we need backpressure so tiny fast-path doesn't starve batch lanes. I propose a soft credit pool per-tenant with decay.
aj: Soft credits + decay seems reasonable. Credits replenish at rate R, consumption per tiny request = 1. If credits <=0 fallback to normal lane.
sam: What about sudden bursts across many tenants? Could still overwhelm coalesce windows. We need a global circuit breaker metric.
chris: Right — add a global tiny_fallback_rate threshold. If exceeded, temporarily widen coalesce windows or rate-limit tiny lanes.
nina: Observability is critical before canary: per-tenant tiny_credit_level, tiny_enq_count, tiny_fallback_count, coalesce_fill_ratio, head_latency_p95. Ops needs dashboards.
maria: Rollout plan I suggest: 1) API hint behind a feature flag. 2) Scheduler accept hint and implement decaying-credit. 3) Expose metrics and a global escape hatch. 4) Canary on low-risk tenants, monitor GPU packing and p95/p99.
aj: Tests: unit simulations for mixed traffic (heavy-tiny vs heavy-batch), integration with fake kernels to verify packing effect, end-to-end latency smoke.
chris: Future work: virtual coalescing where scheduler combines tiny reqs into logical batches without per-request kernel costs — reduces dependence on tiny-lane. That's medium effort.
maria: Open questions: exact credit decay function (exponential vs linear), default credit cap, and threshold for global escape hatch.
elaine: I'll prototype linear decay with configurable half-life param. We can tune from canary telemetry.
ops-bot: CI: branch=feature/tiny-admission-hint build=queued at 3501234600
aj: Ok. Action items: @aj implement minimal hint API PR, @chris implement credit sim and fallback logic, @maria add observability dashboards and canary checklist, @elaine prototype decay math.
maria: Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge the API PR behind flag and we can iterate on decay params after simulation data. :thumbsup:
